correctness.rationale: The full and restricted radial Gram matrices follow exactly from polar Jacobian. Largest eigenvalue: rank-one endpoint limit and shifted-Jacobi Christoffel kernel. Smallest eigenvalue: diagonal scaling to Hilbert moments, explicit bottom-right inverse Hilbert coefficient, and a rank-one reciprocal generalized-eigenvalue limit. Crossover: dominated moment convergence to e^{-x} and explicit 2x2 Laguerre diagonalization. Domain, normalization and nonuniform limits are spelled out in RESULT.md. The 176-assertion standalone checker passed; finite checks are corroboration, not proof.

value.rationale: The central-obscuration limit is a motivated optical harmonic reconstruction regime. All fixed radial orders and azimuthal modes receive a sharp, dimensionally normalized singular-value instability constant, not just an exponent or numerical illustration. The double-scaling two-eigenvalue formula characterizes a nontrivial azimuthal-frequency boundary layer and shows stability recovery at large scaled aperture. These natural exact spectral invariants can inform optical sampling and basis-selection limits without claiming a general noisy inverse theorem.
